title: Can you control your dreams?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss lucid dreaming: what it is (realizing you are dreaming while still asleep), its history from Aristotle and Tibetan Buddhist dream yoga to Dutch psychiatrist Frederik van Eeden, who coined the term, and the Freudian versus physiological explanations of dreams. They cover REM sleep research by Stephen LaBerge at Stanford, including a study where dreamers signaled researchers with prearranged eye movements, and Matthew Walker's theory about the lateral prefrontal cortex. They offer lucid dreaming techniques: keeping a dream journal, MILD (mnemonic induction), looking for dream signs, reality testing, the hands-gazing folk technique, and a light-shining sleep mask device. They share personal dream anecdotes. The episode closes with listener mail about carbon dioxide pipeline safety in Mule Shoe, Texas, and a shout-out to a young listener named Sully.

segments.title: Opening banter and lucid dream setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with Chuck apparently having a lucid dream about flying. They define lucid dreaming as realizing you are dreaming, and note that the debate is over whether people can control dreams. They mention listener requests for this topic.

segments.title: History of lucid dreaming and dream yoga
segments.summary: They discuss Aristotle's early description of lucid dreaming and Tibetan Buddhist dream yoga, which aims for constant awareness including during sleep. They joke about yoga and about monastic life.

segments.title: Psychological versus physiological dream theories
segments.summary: They contrast Freud's psychological view of dreams as expressions of desires, which they call dated, with the physiological camp. They also cover Frederik van Eeden, who coined the term lucid dreaming and kept dream journals.
topics: origin of the term lucid dreaming

segments.title: Stephen LaBerge and lucid dreaming research
segments.summary: They introduce Stephen LaBerge, a Stanford-trained researcher who runs paid workshops. They describe his lab study, in which dreamers signaled researchers with prearranged eye movements while hooked to an EEG.

segments.title: Brain physiology of lucid dreaming
segments.summary: They explain that REM sleep is a paralyzed state with little sensory input. They describe Matthew Walker's theory that the lateral prefrontal cortex, which handles logic, may partly wake during REM and allow dreamers to recognize they are dreaming.

segments.title: Techniques to induce lucid dreams
segments.summary: They offer techniques: keeping a dream journal, MILD (mnemonic induction), looking for dream signs, reality testing, and the folk technique of looking at your hands in a dream. They are skeptical of some of these.

segments.title: Dream mask device and Chuck's and Josh's dream anecdotes
segments.summary: They describe a sleep mask and goggles device that shines a light into the eye when REM is detected as a dream cue. Josh describes his one lucid-like dream about a balloon dog. Chuck describes occasional lucid dreams.

segments.title: Listener mail: carbon dioxide pipeline safety and Mule Shoe
segments.summary: Mason from Ames, Iowa, writes about a 2002 explosion at a carbon dioxide pipeline station near Mule Shoe, Texas, which killed one worker and injured three. Josh and Chuck compare CO2 pipeline incident figures with liquid petroleum figures.

segments.title: Shout-out to Sully and sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck gives a shout-out to Sully, an eleven-year-old listener, and they sign off with the usual listener-mail address and a sponsor line.
